newsitem.title: UK: Levi's to offer buyers customised jeans -UK paper.
newsitem.headline: Levi's to offer buyers customised jeans -UK paper.

text.p: Levi Strauss, the U.S. manufacturer which makes the leading jeans brand, is offering British consumers the chance to have new jeans tailored to their individual shapes, the Financial Times reported on Wednesday.
The marketing project is thought to be the first of its kind in Europe but it has been on trial in the U.S. and Canada for the past 18 months, it added.
Levi Strauss was not immediately available for comment.
The offer, open initially only to women, will enable buyers to be measured up and their details loaded on to a computer in the stores.

The details will be sent to a Levi's factory in Belgium which is equipped with the latest automated cutting machinery, the newspaper said. Delivery will be within 21 days. The jeans, barcoded for identification and to facilitate repeat orders, can be posted directly to the customer or to the point of purchase.
Customers will pay more for the personally-tailored jeans -- 65 pounds for customised jeans compared with an average price of 45 pounds for the regular Levis garment in British stores.

If successful in Britain, Levi's may extend the marketing experiment to some of its larger stores around Europe, the paper quoted the firm as saying. It may also include tailoring men's jeans in the offer if there is sufficient demand.
